messages:
maya: Starting thread — SEA-2 private rack handoff checklist. We landed physical racks yesterday, need a short runbook for the air-gapped seed + customer NAT setup before SOC handover.
ryan: Awesome. Quick questions: are we doing USB shuttle for images or S3-restore via customer jump host?
maya: Customer prefers no external storage. Plan is signed: encrypted USB shuttle, image hash verified, then rsync over isolated jump. Ops requested a one-page verified steps doc.
alex: For GPU capacity, they're asking to start with 8x A100-80GB per rack (2 racks) with room to burst to 4 racks. Cost vs latency tradeoff: 80GB reduces cross-node comms but higher capex.
sophia: For network, customer will run BGP to our mgmt VRF. Important: no egress to internet from compute VLAN — management plane only. We need to validate route leaking rules and TACACS reachability.
jordan: Drafted a quick verification script for NVLink + GPU health, posting snippet: ```bash
# verify nvlink and nv_peer_memory
nvidia-smi topo -m
sudo modprobe nv_peer_mem || true
nvlink --status || echo "nvlink missing"
```
ryan: Nice. Add a step to run a micro-benchmark: 1k tokens inference across intra-rack to measure 95p latency. Use model stub: llama-3-small on quantized profile.
maya: Acceptance criteria proposal: - Control-plane reachable from customer mgmt host - All nodes report green in health API for 30m - 95p inference < 120ms intra-rack, < 220ms cross-rack - KMS integration validated for 10 test keys - KV cache warmup documented
sophia: On KMS: customer uses AWS KMS with no external callouts allowed. We'll bring our private KMS proxy in mgmt VRF and test encrypt/decrypt via proxy only. Need SOC sign-off.
jordan: Edgecases: If the shuttle image hash mismatches, do not accept — escalate to delivery lead + security. Also log USB serial and signer.
ops-bot: NOTE: scheduled maintenance window 2026-04-12T02:00Z for rack power sequencing. Please ack.
maya: We should include a short runbook section for power sequencing (PDUs stagger 30s, bring up master node first, then stateful nodes, then GPU drivers). I'll attach the exact order in the handoff doc.
ryan: For cost ops: recommend enabling aggressive prefix/KV caching on day 1 to cut token cost by ~18% per our benchmarks. Also leave burst policy disabled until health 24h green.
sophia: Networking validation checklist (quick): - BGP session up, correct prefixes announced - No default route leak - DNS resolver pinned to customer internal DNS - NTP sync ok - MTU 9000 verified for RDMA
maya: Final ask: who wants to be on the handoff call with customer tomorrow 14:00 local? @ryan @sophia please. If no objections I'll finalize one-pager and signoff checklist. :thumbsup:
ryan: I can make it.
sophia: Me too.
jordan: I'll be on stand-by for NVLink/driver issues.
maya: Great — I'll post the one-pager in this thread once done and include the USB/hash template and the mini-benchmark command set. Thanks all.
